newsitem.title: CHINA: China economist sees stable domestic interest rate.
newsitem.headline: China economist sees stable domestic interest rate.

text.p: A senior Chinese economist said on Friday he expected China's interest rates to remain fairly stable this year.
"Interest rates are now relatively in conformity with the level of economic development," Qiu Xiaohua, senior economist of the State Statistical Bureau told reporters.
"I personally believe that interest rates in 1997 will be maintained at a more or less stable level," he said.
Some industrialists have called for a further cut in rates after two reductions last year as inflationary pressure eases.
China brought its benchmark retail price inflation to 6.1 percent in 1996, down from a target of 10 percent and 14.8 percent in 1995. It has set a target of 6.0 percent this year.
Chinese Premier Li Peng has said the nation must remain on alert against a resurgence of inflation despite last year's solid record in reining in prices rises.
Many of those pressing for further cuts in interest rates are from loss-making companies in the state sector which has been struggling to repay debt.
Qiu said that China was taking more flexible measures to make economic adjustments.
He added that growing public attention to the nation's interest rate levels was a sign that market mechanisms were taking hold in China.
"This shows that interest rates are playing a greater role in macro-economic policies," he said.
